newsitem.title: INDIA: India state chief applies for bail to avoid arrest.
newsitem.headline: India state chief applies for bail to avoid arrest.

text.p: The chief minister of India's mineral-rich Bihar state, enmeshed in a $280-million corruption scandal, on Thursday applied for bail to prevent arrest, his lawyer said.

The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) this week secured permission from Bihar's governor to prosecute Laloo Prasad Yadav in the "fodder" scandal which dates back to the 1980s and involves the alleged siphoning off of animal welfare funds.
Yadav, who heads Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's Janata Dal party, says he is innocent and has refused to resign and face trial.
Indian law allows a person who expects possible arrest to seek "anticipatory bail" to prevent detention.

Yadav's lawyer, Chitaranjan Kumar Sinha, told reporters in Patna, the state capital, that his client had been falsely implicated in the scandal, which has cast a shadow over the 15-party United Front coalition headed by the Janata Dal.
The court is set to hear the case on Friday.
The CBI had required permission from the state governor to prosecute Yadav, who is among 55 officials and politicians named by the federal police in the fodder scandal.

Laloo Prasad Yadav is meanwhile locked in a party election tussle with challenger Sharad Yadav, no relation of the Bihar chief minister but a key rival in the low-caste Yadav community to which they both belong.
Mutual mistrust over party electoral proceedings has spilled over to courtrooms.
On Thursday, the Supreme Court appointed two senior Janata Dal leaders, Madhu Dandvate and Information and Broadcasting Minister Jaipal Reddy, to hold party elections by July 3.
